questions.q: The word 'Hindu' as reference to the people of Hind (India) was first used by: [1995]
questions.e: The name of India is a corruption of the word Sindhu, the name of the Indus River mentioned in the Rig-Veda. Neighboring Arabs and Iranians uttered 's' as 'h' and called this land Hindu, while Greeks pronounced it as Indus.

questions.q: Who among the following was a Brahmavadini who composed some hymns of the Vedas? [1995]
questions.e: Lopamudra was a Brahmavadini who composed Vedic hymns. Other known Brahmavadini include Vishwawara, Sikta, Nivavari, Ghosha, and Maitreyi.

questions.q: Match List-I (Eras) with List-II (Reckoned from) and select the correct answer: 1️⃣ Vikrama era 2️⃣ Saka era 3️⃣ Gupta era 4️⃣ Kali era [1995]
questions.e: The Vikrama era started in 58 B.C., the Saka era in 78 A.D. (started by Kanishka), the Gupta era in 320 A.D. (started by Chandragupta-I), and the Kali era in 3102 B.C. The 248 A.D. date refers to the Kalachuri era.

questions.q: In Sanskrit plays written during the Gupta period women and Sudras speak: [1995]
questions.e: In Sanskrit plays of the Gupta period, a linguistic distinction was made where women and Sudras spoke Prakrit, while the elite class spoke Sanskrit.

questions.q: The name by which Ashoka is generally referred to in his inscriptions is: [1995]
questions.e: In the Maski rock inscription discovered in 1915, the name Ashoka was found alongside titles like Devanampriya and Priyadarshi, confirming these titles referred to him.

questions.q: The term 'Yavanapriya' mentioned in ancient Sanskrit texts denoted: [1995]
o: a fine variety of Indian Muslim
damsels sent to the Greek court for dance performance
questions.e: Yavanas were Indo-Greeks who had a great liking for Indian pepper. Consequently, pepper became known as 'Yavanapriya' in ancient Sanskrit texts.

questions.q: The concept of Anuvrata was advocated by: [1995]
questions.e: Anuvrata refers to the five main teachings or small vows of Jainism: Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Aparigraha (non-possession), and Brahmacharya (chastity).

questions.q: According to Mimamsa system of philosophy, liberation is possible by means of: [1995]
questions.e: Mimamsa stresses the doctrine of "karma" (action) and ritualism. It posits that liberation is achieved through the performance of Vedic duties and rituals.

questions.q: Bronze icons of Nataraja cast during the Chola period invariably show the deity with: [1995]
questions.e: The four-handed bronze icon of Nataraja is considered the finest example of Chola period sculpture and artistry.

questions.q: According to ancient Indian cosmogonic ideas the sequential order of the cycle of four aeons (yugas) is: [1996]
questions.e: A complete cycle of yugas starts with the Satya Yuga (also called Krita), followed by Treta Yuga, then Dvapara Yuga, and finally ending with Kali Yuga.

questions.q: Which one of the following temples figured in the news regarding the institution of the Devadasi? [1996]
questions.e: A Devadasi was a girl dedicated to the service of a temple deity. In Puri, they were considered the human wives of Lord Jagannath.

questions.q: The river most mentioned in early Vedic literature is: [1996]
questions.e: The Sindhu (Indus River) and the Sapta Sindhu region play a prominent role in the hymns of the Rigveda and early Vedic religion.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a part of early Jains literature? [1996]
questions.e: Therigatha is a part of Buddhist literature, not Jain literature. The other three—Acarangasutra, Sutrakritanga, and Brihatkalpasutra—are early Jain texts.

questions.q: Which of the following were common to both Buddhism and Jainism? 1️⃣ Avoidance of extremities of penance and enjoyment 2️⃣ Indifference to the authority of the Vedas 3️⃣ Denial of efficacy of rituals 4️⃣ Non-injury to animal life [1996]
questions.e: Both religions denied the authority of the Vedas, opposed animal sacrifices (non-injury), and denied the necessity of rituals. However, Buddhism follows the "Middle Path," whereas Jainism advocates extreme penance.

questions.q: In the context of ancient Indian society which one of the following terms does not belong to the category of the other three? [1996]
questions.e: Kula, Vamsa, and Gotra are all terms related to family and lineage, whereas Kosa refers to a treasury.

questions.q: Who among the following is known for his work on medicine during the Gupta period? [1996]
questions.e: Susrutha is the author of the Susrutha Samhita and is renowned as the greatest surgeon of the Gupta period.

questions.q: Which one of the following sculptures invariably used green schist as the medium? [1996]
questions.e: Bharhut sculptures, which often depict Jataka tales (birth stories of the Buddha), were known for using green schist as their primary medium.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer: 1️⃣ Vishakhadatta: Drama 2️⃣ Varahamihira: Astronomy 3️⃣ Charaka: Medicine 4️⃣ Brahmagupta: Mathematics [1996]
questions.e: Vishakhadatta was a dramatist (Mudrarakshasa), Varahamihira was an astronomer, Charaka was a physician (Charaka Samhita), and Brahmagupta was a mathematician.

questions.q: Which one of the following texts of ancient India allows divorce to a wife deserted by her husband? [1996]
questions.e: Kautilya's Arthashastra mentions 'Moksha,' which refers to divorce, and allows for it under certain circumstances such as desertion.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer: 1️⃣ Gupta: Deogarh 2️⃣ Chandella: Khajuraho 3️⃣ Chalukya: Badami 4️⃣ Pallava: Panamalai [1997]
questions.e: The Guptas are associated with Deogarh temples, the Chandellas built Khajuraho, the Chalukyas ruled from Badami (Vatapi), and the Pallavas are associated with Panamalai and Kanchi.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding Ashoka stone pillars is incorrect? [1997]
o: The shaft of pillars is tapering in shape
These are parts of architectural structures
questions.e: Ashoka's stone pillars were independent monolithic structures meant to spread the message of Dhamma; they were not integrated parts of larger architectural buildings.

questions.q: Which one of the following scripts of ancient India was written from right to left? [1997]
questions.e: Kharosthi script, used in Ashoka's edicts in the northwest, was written from right to left. It was deciphered by James Prinsep using bilingual Indo-Greek coins.

questions.q: The famous dialogue between Nachiketa and Yama is mentioned in the: [1997]
questions.e: The Kathopanishad contains the profound conversation between the young seeker Nachiketa and Yamraj (the God of Death), who acts as his Guru.

questions.q: Milindapanho is in the form of a dialogue between the king Menander and Buddhist monk: [1997]
questions.e: Milindapanho (Questions of Milinda) is a recording of the philosophical dialogue between the Indo-Greek King Milinda and the Buddhist sage Nagasena.

questions.q: Which one of the following edicts mentions the personal name of Ashoka? [1997]
questions.e: While most inscriptions use titles, the Maski, Gurjara, Nettur, and Udegolam inscriptions are significant because they mention the personal name "Ashoka."

questions.q: The following map shows four of the sixteen Mahajanapadas that existed in ancient India: A, B, C, D. These respectively are: [1997]
questions.e: Matsya was in the Jaipur region, Avanti in Ujjain, Vatsa at Kausambi, and Anga in the Gangetic valley.

questions.q: In the Mahayana Buddhism, the Bodhisatva Avalokitesvara was also known as: [1997]
questions.e: Avalokitesvara, the bodhisattva of compassion, is also known as Padmapāni ("Holder of the Lotus") or Lokeśvara ("Lord of the World").

questions.q: The silver coins issued by the Guptas were called: [1997]
questions.e: Silver coins of the Gupta period were known as Rupaka. During this time, 16 silver Rupakas were equal in value to one gold coin.

questions.q: Match List-I (Author) with List-II (Text): 1️⃣ Varahamihira: Brihat-Samhita 2️⃣ Vishakhadatta: Devi-Chandraguptam 3️⃣ Sudraka: Mrichchha-Katikam 4️⃣ Bilhana: Vikramankadeva-Charita [1997]
questions.e: Varahamihira wrote Brihat-Samhita, Vishakhadatta wrote Devi-Chandraguptam, Sudraka wrote Mrichchha-Katikam, and Bilhana wrote Vikramankadeva-Charita.

questions.q: Which one of the following was a corporation of merchants in ancient India? [1997]
questions.e: Manigramam was a large and influential guild or corporation of South Indian merchants active during the 10th-12th Century CE.

questions.q: The Badami rock inscription of Pulakesin I is dated in the Saka year 465. If the same were to be dated in Vikrama Samvat, the year would be: [1997]
questions.e: To convert from Saka era (78 AD) to Vikrama era (58 BC), one must add the differences: 465 (Saka year) + 78 + 58 = 601 Vikrama Samvat.

questions.q: Many of the Greeks, Kushanas and Shakas embraced Buddhism rather than Hinduism because: [1998]
o: Buddhism provided easier access to Indian society
Buddhism was in the ascendant at that time
they had renounced the policy of war and violence
caste-ridden Hinduism did not attract them
questions.e: Foreign invaders like the Greeks and Shakas were drawn to Buddhism because its egalitarian nature was more appealing than the rigid caste system of Hinduism.

questions.q: The Ashoka major rock edicts which tell us about the Sangam Kingdom include rock edicts: [1998]
questions.e: Major Rock Edicts II and XIII of Ashoka are historical sources that mention the southern Sangam kingdoms of the Cholas, Pandyas, Satyaputras, and Keralaputras.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Mrichchakatikam-Shudraka 2️⃣ Buddhacharita-Vasuvandhu 3️⃣ Mudrarakshasha-Vishakadatta 4️⃣ Harshacharita-Banabhatta [1998]
questions.e: Mrichchakatikam was written by Shudraka, Mudrarakshasa by Vishakhadatta, and Harshacharita by Banabhatta. Buddhacharita was written by Ashvaghosh, not Vasuvandhu.

questions.q: What is the correct chronological order in which the following appeared in India? 1️⃣ Gold coins 2️⃣ Punch marked silver coins 3️⃣ Iron plough 4️⃣ Urban culture [1998]
questions.e: The order is: Urban culture (Indus Valley, 2500 BCE), Iron plough (c. 700 BC), Punch marked coins (7th-6th century BC), and Gold coins (Indo-Greeks, c. 200 BC).

questions.q: Assertion (A): According to Ashoka's edicts social harmony among the people was more important than religious devotion. Reason (R): He spread ideas of equity instead of promotion of religion. [1998]
o: Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Ashoka prioritized social harmony and equity (Dhamma) over specific religious dogma, using his edicts to spread these ethical principles across his empire.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Lothal: Ancient dockyard 2️⃣ Sarnath: First Sermon of Buddha 3️⃣ Rajgir: Lion capital of Ashoka 4️⃣ Nalanda: Great seat of Buddhist learning [1998]
questions.e: Lothal had a dockyard, Sarnath was where Buddha gave his first sermon, and Nalanda was a major learning center. The Lion Capital of Ashoka is at Sarnath, not Rajgir.

questions.q: Which one of the following ancient Indian records is the earliest royal order to preserve food-grains to be utilised during the crises in the country? [1998]
questions.e: The Sohgaura copper-plate is a Maurya-era record that mentions famine relief efforts and instructions for grain storage.

questions.q: The concept of Eight fold path forms the theme of: [1998]
questions.e: The Noble Eightfold Path is a central teaching introduced in the Dharma Chakra Pravartana Sutta, representing the way to end suffering.

questions.q: The given map relates to: [1998]
o: Samudragupta after the close of his South Indian campaign.
Empire of Thaneswar on the eve of Harsha's accession.
Ashoka towards close of his reign.
Kanishka at the time of his death.
questions.e: The map shows the extent of the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka, covering most of the subcontinent from Afghanistan to northern Kerala and Andhra.

questions.q: From the third century AD when the Hun invasion ended the Roman Empire, the Indian merchants relied more and more on the: [1999]
questions.e: Following the decline of the Roman Empire in the 3rd century AD, Indian trade shifted focus significantly toward South-East Asia.

questions.q: The following persons came to India at one time or another: 1️⃣ Fa-Hien 2️⃣ I-Tsing 3️⃣ Megasthanese 4️⃣ Hieun-Tsang. The correct chronological sequence of their visits is: [1999]
questions.e: Chronology: Megasthenes (c. 300 BC), Fa-Hien (405-411 CE), Hiuen-Tsang (630-645 CE), and I-Tsing (671-695 CE).

questions.q: Which one of the following was initially the most powerful city state of India in the 6th century B.C.? [1999]
questions.e: Among the 16 Mahajanapadas, Magadha ultimately emerged as the most powerful state under the Haryanka dynasty in the 6th century BC.

questions.q: The Indo-Greek Kingdom set up in north Afghanistan in the beginning of the second century B.C. was: [1999]
questions.e: Bactria was an ancient civilization located between the Hindu Kush and Amu Darya, where an Indo-Greek kingdom was established.

questions.q: The term 'Aryan' denotes: [1999]
questions.e: 'Aryan' is a linguistic term used to describe a speech group of Indo-European origin; it is not defined by ethnicity.

questions.q: Which one of the following ports handled the North Indian trade during the Gupta period? [1999]
questions.e: Tamralipti, located on the Bay of Bengal, was a major trade hub during the Gupta period for routes to China, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The Aham and Puram poems of the Padinen Kilukanakku group formed a continuation of the Sangam composition. Reason (R): They were included under the post-Sangam works as against the Sangam works proper. [2000]
o: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
questions.e: The Kilukanakku works consist of post-Sangam poems that continue the themes of the original Sangam compositions.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The emphasis of Jainism on non-violence (ahimsa) prevented agriculturalists from embracing Jainism. Reason (R): Cultivation involved killing of insects and pests. [2000]
o: Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Jainism's strict vow of Ahimsa made farming difficult for its followers, as the act of tilling the soil inevitably kills insects and microorganisms.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The origin of feudal system in ancient India can be traced to military campaigns. Reason (R): There was considerable expansion of the feudal system during the Gupta period. [2000]
o: Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: While both statements are true—feudal origins are linked to military grants and the system grew in the Gupta era—one is not the direct causal explanation of the other.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Ashoka annexed Kalinga to the Mauryan Empire. Reason (R): Kalinga controlled the land and sea routes to South India. [2000]
o: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Ashoka conquered Kalinga in 261 BC because of its strategic importance in controlling trade routes to South India.

questions.q: The practice of military governorship was first introduced in India by the: [2000]
questions.e: The Greeks were the first to introduce military governorship (the office of 'strategos') in India.

questions.q: Which one of the following dynasties was ruling over North India at the time of Alexander's invasion? [2000]
questions.e: When Alexander invaded India in 326 BC, the Nanda dynasty was in power in North India.

questions.q: Hoysala monuments are found in: [2001]
questions.e: The Hoysala capital was initially at Belur and later moved to Halebid; both sites are famous for their Hoysala-style monuments.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched? [2001]
o: The Marathas - Pahari School of Painting
The Kushans - Gandhra School of Art
questions.e: The Kushan period is famous for the Gandhara School of Art. Painted Greyware is Vedic, Ajanta is Gupta, and Pahari art began in the Mughal era.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Harshavardhana convened the Prayag Assembly. Reason (R): He wanted to popularize only the Mahayana form of Buddhism. [2001]
o: Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Harsha held an assembly at Kannauj to popularize Mahayana Buddhism, but the Prayag assembly was generally to distribute wealth and enhance his own popularity.

questions.q: Which one of the Chola kings conquered Ceylon? [2001]
questions.e: Rajendra Chola I conquered all of Ceylon in 1017, whereas Rajaraja I had only conquered the northern half previously.

questions.q: Who among the following presided over the Buddhist Council held during the reign of Kanishka at Kashmir? [2001]
questions.e: The fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir was presided over by Vasumitra and Ashvaghosh.

questions.q: Which one of the following animals was not represented on seals and terracotta art of the Harappan culture? [2001]
questions.e: While elephants, rhinos, and tigers appear on Harappan seals, the cow, horse, camel, and lion were not depicted.

questions.q: Match List-I (Ancient site) with List-II (Archaeological finding): 1️⃣ Lothal: Dockyard 2️⃣ Kalibangan: Ploughed field 3️⃣ Dholavira: 10 large signs of script 4️⃣ Banawali: Terracotta replica of plough [2002]
questions.e: Lothal is known for its dockyard, Kalibangan for a ploughed field, Dholavira for its script inscription, and Banawali for a terracotta plough.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is not correct? [2002]
o: Khajuraho temples were built under Chandela kings.
Hoysaleswara temple is dedicated to Siva.
The statue of Gomateshwara at Shravana Belagola represents the last Tirthankara of Jains.
India's largest Buddhist monastery is in Arunachal Pradesh.
questions.e: The Gomateshwara statue represents Bahubali, not a Tirthankara. The Tawang Monastery in Arunachal is India's largest.

questions.q: In ancient Indian Buddhist monasteries, a ceremony called Pavarana used to be held. It was the: [2002]
o: gathering of Buddhist monks on the next day to the full-moon day of Ashadha when they take up a fixed abode for the next four months of the rainy season
confession by monks of their offences committed during their stay in the monasteries during the rainy season
ceremony of initiation of new person into the Buddhist Sangha in which the head is shaved and when yellow robes are offered
occasion to elect the Sanghparinayaka and two speakers one on Dhamma and the other on Vinaya
questions.e: Pavarana marks the end of the rainy season (Vassa) when monks come together to confess and atone for offenses committed during their retreat.

questions.q: The ancient Indian play Mudrarakshasa of Visakhadutt has its subject on: [2002]
o: a romantic story of an Aryan prince and a tribal woman
the story of the power struggle between two Aryan clans
the court intrigues at the time of Chandragupta Maurya
a conflict between Gods and Demons of ancient Hindu lore
questions.e: Mudrarakshasa by Vishakhadatta narrates how Chandragupta Maurya rose to power in Northern India through political strategy.

questions.q: Emperor Harsha's southward march was stopped on the Narmada river by: [2003]
questions.e: The Chalukya king Pulakesin II defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada, stopping his expansion into South India.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Cholas defeated Pandya and Chera rulers and established their domination over peninsular India in the early medieval times. 2️⃣ The Cholas sent an expedition against Sailendra empire of South-East Asia and conquered some of the areas. Which is/are correct? [2003]
questions.e: The Cholas dominated South India by defeating the Pandyas and Cheras and also projected naval power to conquer parts of the Sailendra kingdom in SE Asia.

questions.q: 'Mrichchhakatika' an ancient Indian book written by Shudraka deals with: [2003]
o: the victory of Chandragupta II over the Shaka Kshatrapas of western India
the love affairs between a Gupta king and a princess of Kamarupa
the love affair of a rich merchant with the daughter of a courtesan
the military expeditions and exploits of Samudragupta
questions.e: This Sanskrit play tells the story of the merchant Charudatta and his love for Vasantasena, a wealthy courtesan.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Vardhaman Mahavira's mother was the daughter of Lichchhavi chief Chetaka 2️⃣ Gautama Buddha's mother was a princess from the Koshalan dynasty 3️⃣ Parshvanatha, the twenty-third Tirthankara, belonged to Benaras. Which is/are correct? [2003]
questions.e: Mahavira's mother Trishala was the sister, not the daughter, of Chetaka. Buddha's mother was a Koshalan princess, and Parshvanatha was from Benaras.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha was assassinated by Pushyamitra Sunga. 2️⃣ The last Sunga king, Devabhuti was assassinated by Vasudeva Kanva. 3️⃣ The last ruler of the Kanva dynasty was deposed by the Andhras. [2003]
questions.e: All three statements accurately describe the successive transitions of power in post-Mauryan North India.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien attended the fourth Great Buddhist Council held by Kanishka. 2️⃣ The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen-Tsang met Harsha and found him to be antagonistic to Buddhism. [2004]
questions.e: Fa-Hien visited during the Gupta era (not Kanishka's), and Hiuen-Tsang found Harsha to be a great supporter of Buddhism, not antagonistic.

questions.q: With reference to ancient Jainism, which one of the following statements is correct? [2004]
o: Jainism enjoyed the patronage of the Kalinga king Kharaavela in the first century BC.
The Jainas who remained under the leadership of Bhadrabahu were called Shvetambaras after the council held at Pataliputra.
Jainism was spread in South India under the leadership of Sthalabahu.
In the initial stage of Jainism, the Jainas worshipped images unlike the Buddhist.
questions.e: Jainism spread south under Bhadrabahu (whose followers were Digambaras). King Kharavela was a famous patron of Jainism.

questions.q: Which one of the following four Vedas contains an account of magical charms and spells? [2004]
questions.e: The Atharvaveda is distinct for its focus on magical formulas, charms, and spells to ward off evil and disease.

questions.q: Who among the following was not a contemporary of the other three? [2005]
questions.e: Bimbisara, Buddha, and Prasenjit were all contemporaries in the 6th century BC. Milinda (Menander) ruled much later in the 2nd century BC.

questions.q: Who among the following laid the foundation of Rashtrakuta Empire? [2006]
questions.e: Dantidurga, a former feudatory of the Chalukyas, founded the Rashtrakuta Empire in 753 CE.

questions.q: Between which of the following was the ancient town of Takshasila located? [2006]
questions.e: Takshashila (Taxila) was historically situated between the Indus (Sindhu) and Jhelum (Vitasta) rivers.

questions.q: With reference to the invaders in ancient India, which one of the following is the correct chronological order? [2006]
questions.e: The sequence of major foreign invasions was Greeks (326 BC), followed by the Sakas (90 BC), and then the Kushanas (45 AD).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Ikshvaku rulers of Southern India were antagonistic towards Buddhism. 2️⃣ The Pala rulers of Eastern India were patrons of Buddhism. Which is/are correct? [2006]
questions.e: Palas were famous patrons, but Ikshvaku inscriptions show they supported Buddhism by funding viharas, making statement 1 incorrect.

questions.q: The Allahabad Pillar inscription is associated with which one of the following? [2006]
questions.e: Known as the Prayaga-prasasti, it was composed by Harisena in praise of the Gupta emperor Samudragupta.

questions.q: What does Baudhayan theorem (Baudhayan Sulva Sutras) relate to? [2008]
o: Calculation of the value of pi
Lengths of sides of a right angled triangle
questions.e: The Baudhayan Sulva Sutras contain early statements of what is now commonly known as the Pythagoras theorem.

questions.q: Anekantavada is a core theory and philosophy of which one of the following? [2009]
questions.e: Anekantavada is a fundamental Jain doctrine regarding the 'many-sidedness of reality' and pluralism.

questions.q: There are only two known examples of cave paintings of the Gupta period in ancient India. One is Ajanta; where is the other? [2010]
questions.e: Apart from Ajanta, the Bagh caves provide the only other surviving example of Gupta-era cave paintings.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most convincing explanation for the early maritime history of Bay of Bengal? [2011-1]
o: India had better ship-building technology than other countries
Southern Indian rulers always patronized traders and monks
Monsoon winds across the Bay of Bengal facilitated sea voyages
questions.e: The seasonal monsoon winds were the primary geographical factor that allowed ancient and medieval sailors to cross the Bay of Bengal for trade.

questions.q: The Jain philosophy holds that the world is created and maintained by: [2011-1]
questions.e: Jainism rejects the idea of a creator deity; instead, it teaches that the universe is eternal and governed by universal natural laws.

questions.q: Regarding the Indus Valley Civilization: 1️⃣ It was predominantly a secular civilization; religious elements did not dominate. 2️⃣ During this period, cotton was used for manufacturing textiles in India. [2011-1]
questions.e: The civilization was urban and secular in nature. Archaeological evidence also confirms early cotton cultivation and textile production.

questions.q: The "Dharma" and "Rita" depict a central Idea of ancient Vedic civilization. 1️⃣ Dharma was a conception of obligations and duties. 2️⃣ Rita was the fundamental moral law governing the universe. [2011-1]
questions.e: Dharma focused on human social and personal duties, while Rita referred to the cosmic order and moral laws of the universe.

questions.q: With reference to the scientific progress of ancient India, which are correct? 1️⃣ Specialized surgical instruments were used by 1st century AD. 2️⃣ Transplant of internal organs began by 3rd century AD. 3️⃣ Sine of an angle was known in 5th century AD. 4️⃣ Cyclic quadrilaterals were known in 7th century AD. [2012-1]
questions.e: Ancient India excelled in surgery and math, knowing about sine and cyclic quadrilaterals; however, there is no evidence of internal organ transplants by the 3rd century.

questions.q: Which of the following was/were common to both Buddhism and Jainism? 1️⃣ Avoidance of extremities of penance and enjoyment 2️⃣ Indifference to the authority of the Vedas 3️⃣ Denial of efficacy of rituals [2012-1]
questions.e: Both religions rejected Vedic authority and rituals. However, Buddhism specifically advocated the "Middle Path," while Jainism practiced extreme penance.

questions.q: The Nagara, the Dravida and the Vesara are the: [1995, 2012-1]
o: three main linguistic divisions of Indian languages
three main racial groups of the Indian subcontinent
three main musical Gharanas prevalent in India
three main styles of Indian temple architecture
questions.e: These represent the three primary styles of temple architecture: Nagara (North), Dravida (South), and Vesara (Hybrid).

questions.q: Lord Buddha's 'Bhumisparsha Mudra' symbolizes: [2012-1]
o: Both the statements (a) and (b) are correct
Buddha's reminder that all arise from and dissolve into the Earth
Buddha's calling of the Earth to witness his purity and chastity despite the temptations of Mara
Buddha's calling of the Earth to watch over Mara
questions.e: This gesture represents the moment of enlightenment where Buddha calls the Earth to testify to his worthiness and purity against the temptations of Mara.

questions.q: The religion of early Vedic Aryans was primarily of: [2012-1]
questions.e: Early Vedic religion focused on the worship of natural forces and the performance of Yajnas (sacrificial rituals).

questions.q: With reference to the guilds (Shreni) of ancient India: 1️⃣ Every guild was registered with the king as the chief authority. 2️⃣ Wages, work rules, and prices were fixed by the guild. 3️⃣ The guild had judicial powers over its members. [2012-1]
questions.e: Guilds were self-regulating economic units that set their own rules for wages and prices and held judicial authority over their own members.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a Chaitya and a Vihara? [2013-1]
o: Chaitya is a place of worship, while Vihara is the dwelling place of the monks
Vihara is a place of worship, while Chaitya is the dwelling place
Chaitya is the stupa at the far end of the cave, while Vihara is the hall axial to it
There is no material difference between the two
questions.e: Chaityas were prayer halls containing stupas for large numbers of devotees, while Viharas served as residences for wandering monks.

questions.q: Regarding the Sankhya school: 1️⃣ Sankhya does not accept the theory of rebirth or transmigration. 2️⃣ Sankhya holds that self-knowledge leads to liberation. [2013-1]
questions.e: Sankhya philosophy accepts the concept of rebirth and teaches that kaivalya (liberation) is achieved solely through self-knowledge.

questions.q: Which one of the following describes best the concept of Nirvana in Buddhism? [2013-1]
o: A state of bliss and rest
The extinction of the flame of desire
A mental stage beyond all comprehension
questions.e: Nirvana literally means 'to blow out,' referring to the extinguishing of the fires of greed, hatred, and delusion.

questions.q: Which of the following characterizes the people of Indus Civilization? 1️⃣ They possessed great palaces and temples. 2️⃣ They worshipped both male and female deities. 3️⃣ They employed horse-drawn chariots in warfare. [2013-1]
questions.e: They worshipped figures like the Mother Goddess and a prototype of Shiva. They lacked great temples/palaces and there is no evidence of horse-chariots in war.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are applicable to Jain doctrine? 1️⃣ The surest way of annihilating Karma is to practice penance. 2️⃣ Every object, even the smallest particle has a soul. 3️⃣ Karma is the bane of the soul and must be ended. [2013-1]
questions.e: Jainism teaches that karma is subtle matter that taints the soul in every object; it must be removed through penance to achieve liberation.

questions.q: With reference to Indian rock-cut architecture: 1️⃣ Badami caves are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves. 2️⃣ Barabar rock-cut caves were made for Ajivikas by Chandragupta Maurya. 3️⃣ At Ellora, caves were made for different faiths. [2013-1]
questions.e: Barabar caves are the oldest (built for Ajivikas under Ashoka/Mauryas). Ellora is unique for housing Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain caves together.

questions.q: The Chinese traveller Yuan Chwang recorded that: 1️⃣ Roads and river-routes were immune from robbery. 2️⃣ Ordeals by fire, water and poison were used to determine innocence. 3️⃣ Tradesmen had to pay duties at ferries and barrier stations. [2013-1]
questions.e: Yuan Chwang noted that while punishment was strict (including ordeals), travel was not entirely safe from robbery. He confirmed the payment of trade duties.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the 'Tribhanga' dance pose? [2013-1]
o: Movements of body, face and hands are used to express oneself or tell a story
A little smile, slightly curved waist and certain hand gestures are emphasized to express love
Facial expressions, hand gestures and make-up are combined to symbolize characters
One leg is bent and the body is slightly but oppositely curved at waist and neck
questions.e: Tribhanga is a favorite posture in Indian art, where the body is curved in three places: the neck, waist, and knee.

questions.q: Which of the following historical places is/are also known for mural paintings? 1️⃣ Ajanta Caves 2️⃣ Lepakshi Temple 3️⃣ Sanchi Stupa [2013-1]
questions.e: Ajanta and Lepakshi are both famous for their murals. Sanchi is renowned for its sculptures but does not have mural paintings.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of sculptures: 1️⃣ Ajanta: Mahaparinirvana of Buddha 2️⃣ Mount Abu: Varaha Avatar of Vishnu 3️⃣ Mamallapuram: Arjuna's Penance. Which are correctly matched? [2014-1]
questions.e: The Mahaparinirvana is a famous Ajanta Cave 17 relief, and Arjuna's Penance is at Mamallapuram. The Varaha Avatar relief is also at Mamallapuram, not Mount Abu.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of Buddhist shrines: 1️⃣ Tabo monastery: Spiti Valley 2️⃣ Lhotsava Lhakhang temple: Zanskar Valley 3️⃣ Alchi temple complex: Ladakh. Which are correct? [2014-1]
questions.e: Tabo is in Spiti and Alchi is in Ladakh. Lhotsava Lhakhang is located in Nako (Himachal Pradesh), not Zanskar.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs does not form part of the six systems of Indian Philosophy? [2014-1]
questions.e: The six orthodox systems are Sankhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta. Lokayata and Kapalika are heterodox or non-Vedic.

questions.q: The national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from: [2014-1]
questions.e: The phrase 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth Alone Triumphs) is a quote from the Mundaka Upanishad.

questions.q: Which of the following Kingdoms were associated with the life of the Buddha? 1️⃣ Avanti 2️⃣ Gandhara 3️⃣ Kosala 4️⃣ Magadha [2014-1]
questions.e: Buddha was born in Lumbini (Kosala) and died in Kusinara (Magadha). He never visited Avanti or Gandhara (modern Pakistan).

questions.q: Which one among the following was made earliest? [2015-1]
questions.e: The Dhauli elephant dates to Ashoka's reign (c. 250 BC), much earlier than the Gupta-era Udayagiri (5th C), Pallava-era Mahabalipuram (7th C), or Lingaraja (11th C).

questions.q: Which one of the following books of ancient India has the love story of the son of the founder of Sunga dynasty? [2016-1]
questions.e: Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitra tells the story of King Agnimitra (son of Pushyamitra Sunga) and his love for the maiden Malavika.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Eripatti: Land for village tank maintenance 2️⃣ Taniyurs: Villages donated to Brahmins 3️⃣ Ghatikas: Colleges attached to temples. Which are correctly matched? [2016-1]
questions.e: Eripatti was land for tank maintenance and Ghatikas were temple colleges. Taniyurs were actually large villages administered as single units.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Sautrantika and Sammitiya were the sects of Jainism. 2️⃣ Sarvastivadin held that the constituents of phenomena existed forever in a latent form. [2017-1]
questions.e: Sautrantika and Sammitiya are Buddhist sects, not Jain. The Sarvastivadin Buddhist sect believed that everything exists in the past, present, and future.

questions.q: The painting of Bodhisattva Padmapani is one of the most famous paintings at: [2017-1]
questions.e: The magnificent Padmapani Bodhisattva mural is located in Cave No. 1 of the Ajanta Caves.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are famous for Sun temples? 1️⃣ Arasavalli 2️⃣ Amarakantak 3️⃣ Omkareshwar [2017-1]
questions.e: Arasavalli in Andhra Pradesh houses a famous Sun temple. Omkareshwar and Amarakantak are famous for temples dedicated to Shiva.

questions.q: Regarding Rigvedic Aryans vs Indus Valley people: 1️⃣ Aryans used helmets/coats of mail; Indus people did not. 2️⃣ Aryans knew gold, silver, copper; Indus people knew only copper and iron. 3️⃣ Aryans domesticated horses; Indus people were unaware of them. [2017-1]
questions.e: Indus people knew gold and silver (but not iron). While debates exist, official views suggest Harappans were not aware of horses, unlike the Aryans.

questions.q: Which one of the following was a very important seaport in the Kakatiya kingdom? [2017-1]
questions.e: Motupalli was a major seaport in the Kakatiya kingdom, flourishing under the reign of King Ganapati.

questions.q: With reference to the religious practices in India, the "Sthanakvasi" sect belongs to: [2018-1]
questions.e: Sthanakvasi is a sub-sect of the Svetambara school of Jainism.

questions.q: With reference to Indian history, who among the following is a future Buddha, yet to come to save the world? [2018-1]
questions.e: Maitreya is prophesied to be the future Buddha who will eventually appear to purify the world with his teachings.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of Craft vs Heritage: 1️⃣ Puthukkuli shawls: Tamil Nadu 2️⃣ Sujni embroidery: Maharashtra 3️⃣ Uppada Jamdani saris: Karnataka. Which are correct? [2018-1]
questions.e: Puthukkuli shawls are from Tamil Nadu. Sujni embroidery is from Bihar, and Uppada Jamdani saris are from Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of Tradition vs State: 1️⃣ Chapchar Kut festival: Mizoram 2️⃣ Khongjom Parba ballad: Manipur 3️⃣ Thang-Ta dance: Sikkim. Which are correct? [2018-1]
questions.e: Chapchar Kut is Mizoram's festival, and Khongjom Parba is a Manipuri ballad. Thang-Ta is a martial dance from Manipur, not Sikkim.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a Harappan Site? [2019-1]
questions.e: Sohagaura is a Mauryan site known for its copper-plate inscription, not a site of the Harappan civilization.

questions.q: In which relief sculpture inscription is 'Ranyo Ashoka' (King Ashoka) mentioned along with a stone portrait? [2019-1]
questions.e: Excavations at Kanagahalli (part of the Sannati site) in Karnataka revealed a portrait of Ashoka with the Brahmi inscription "Ranyo Ashoka."

questions.q: Which of the following are features of Mahayana Buddhism? 1️⃣ Deification of the Buddha 2️⃣ Treading the path of Bodhisattvas 3️⃣ Image worship and rituals [2019-1]
questions.e: Mahayana Buddhism is characterized by viewing Buddha as a deity, the ideal of the Bodhisattva, and the practice of image worship.

questions.q: With reference to forced labour (Vishti) in the Gupta period: [2019-1]
o: It was totally absent in the Madhya Pradesh and Kathiawar regions.
It was considered a source of income for the State, a sort of tax paid by the people.
The eldest son of the labourer was sent as the forced labourer.
The forced labourer as entitled to weekly wages.
questions.e: Vishti was a form of forced labor considered a legitimate state tax, particularly prevalent in the MP and Kathiawar regions of the Gupta Empire.

questions.q: Building 'Kalyaana Mandapas' was a notable feature in the temple construction in the kingdom of: [2019-1]
questions.e: The Vijayanagara style of temple architecture introduced the 'Kalyan Mandap,' a central hall dedicated to the symbolic marriage of deities.

questions.q: With reference to the cultural history of India, which one of the following is the correct description of the term 'paramitas'? [2020-1]
o: Perfections whose attainment led to the Bodhisattva path
Philosophical schools that did not accept the authority of Vedas.
Powerful merchant guilds of early medieval south India.
The earliest Dharmashastra texts written in aphoristic (sutra) style.
questions.e: Paramitas refer to the spiritual perfections (like Prajna Paramita) in Mahayana Buddhism that a Bodhisattva must master.

questions.q: With reference to the scholars of ancient India: 1️⃣ Panini is associated with Pushyamitra Shunga 2️⃣ Amarasimha is associated with Harshavardhana 3️⃣ Kalidasa is associated with Chandra Gupta-II [2020-1]
questions.e: Kalidasa and Amarasimha were both 'navratnas' in the court of Chandragupta II. Panini lived much earlier (5th-6th C BC) than Pushyamitra Sunga (2nd C BC).

questions.q: With reference to religious history: 1️⃣ Sthaviravadins belong to Mahayana Buddhism. 2️⃣ Lokottaravadin sect was an offshoot of Mahasanghika sect. 3️⃣ The deification of Buddha by Mahasanghikas fostered Mahayana Buddhism. [2020-1]
questions.e: Sthaviravadins were Hinayanists. Lokottaravadins were indeed an offshoot of the Mahasanghikas, who helped pioneer the Mahayana tradition.

questions.q: Chronological order of events: 1️⃣ Rise of Pratiharas under King Bhoja 2️⃣ Establishment of Pallava power under Mahendravarman - I 3️⃣ Establishment of Chola power under Parantaka-I 4️⃣ Pala dynasty founded by Gopala [2020-1]
questions.e: Sequence: Mahendravarman-I (590-630), Gopala (750), King Bhoja (836-885), and Parantaka-I (907-953).

questions.q: What is the nature of 'Hundi' referred to in post-Harsha sources? [2020-1]
o: An advisory issued by the king to his subordinates
An order from the feudal lord to his subordinates
A diary to be maintained for daily accounts
questions.e: A Hundi was a financial instrument serving as a bill of exchange, allowing money deposited in one place to be claimed in another.

questions.q: The terms "kulyavapa" and "dronavapa" denote: [2020-1]
questions.e: These were common units for the measurement of land used during the Gupta period, particularly in the Bengal region.

questions.q: Which ruler advised: "Whosoever praises his religious sect or blames other sects... rather injures his own sect very severely"? [2020-1]
questions.e: This famous inscription reflects Ashoka's policy of Dhamma, emphasizing religious tolerance and mutual respect among all sects.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Bhilsa: Madhya Pradesh 2️⃣ Dwarasamudra: Maharashtra 3️⃣ Girinagar: Gujarat 4️⃣ Sthaneshwara: Uttar Pradesh. Which are correct? [2020-1]
questions.e: Bhilsa (Vidisha) is in MP and Girinagar is in Gujarat. Dwarasamudra is in Karnataka, and Sthaneshwara is in Haryana.

questions.q: In the Gupta period, the towns Ghantasala, Kadura and Chaul were well known as: [2020-1]
o: places of exquisite stone art and architecture
questions.e: These were significant coastal towns and ports that facilitated maritime trade during the Gupta era.

questions.q: Match the following pairs: 1️⃣ Parivrajaka: Renunciant and Wanderer 2️⃣ Shramana: Priest with high status 3️⃣ Upasaka: Lay follower of Buddhism. Which are correct? [2020-1]
questions.e: A Parivrajaka is a wandering seeker, and an Upasaka is a lay Buddhist. Shramanas were ascetics who actually challenged the status and rituals of Brahmanical priests.
